page.layout: One printed page (left, p. 348): running text in one column, with the running head at the top and a catchword at the foot right. Right of it, the edge of a second printed page, cropped and out of focus: a narrow column of marginal notes along its left edge and a few partial lines of text. The right page is not transcribed beyond the partial lines below, because it is too damaged to read.

main_text.p: impium: qua præsignificatione ex sigillo visa, silent & horrescunt omnia in cœlo præ admiratione, donec mandata executionis à Deo sigillatim dantur administris eius. Sic transitur ad tertium membrum, de malorum quibus Deus mundum iustissimè statuit affligere, executione.
Hæc autè executio primùm generatim præparatur ad v. vsque 6. huius capitis. Deinde minutatim, secundùm administrorum ordinem exponitur in seqq.

Ad præparandam executionem narrantur ista: primum qui administri ac instrumenta illius: v. 2. Deinde quod opus tum principis Angelorum hac executionem informantis, (v. 3.4, 5.)tum administrorum eius. v. 6.

Narratio rerum singularium, quas Angeli sex numero operati sunt duo ordine, exponuntur deinceps, ad v. 20. vsque capitis sequentis: Concluditur verò indicatione euentus, qui ex his rebus gestis apud mundum confecutus est: duobus vltimis. A v. igitur 7. capitis octaui narratur quomodo quatuor primis Angelis clangentibus ignis decidat, mare turbetur, aquæ amarescant, & stellæ obtenebrentur.
main_text.head: Cap. IX.
main_text.p: Quinto Angelo clangente, locusta vastatrices prodeunt: vsque ad v. 13. Sextus autem clangens equites educit humanum genus deuastantes: vsque ad v. 20. Postremò communis euentus, in mundo ex antegressis excutitionibus inemendabili, exponitur v. 20. & 21.

page.notes: Right page: cropped and blurred at the binding edge. Its marginal notes and partial text lines could not be read reliably and are not transcribed. The faint lines showing through below the text on the left page are show-through and are omitted. Catchword "PROPHE" is cut off at the edge; the reading is uncertain. The left page's first line is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Possible spelling "excutitionibus" in the Cap. IX paragraph is uncertain.
